newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED SOFTER ON WEDNESDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED SOFTER ON WEDNESDAY.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market opened short on Wednesday but dealers said liquidity was expected to improve during the day on the back of treasury bill maturities, and short-term trading rates were quoted softer compared to Tuesday's levels.
"We were Z$68 million short under yesterday's (Tuesday's) date but we're expecting Z$271 million (worth of) treasury bill maturities today," one dealer said.

He said discount houses were selling treasury bills in a 17.50 to 17.75 percentage range from Tuesday's 17.80 percent while NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at around 18.50 percent from 19.50 percent and sold at 18.25, slightly down from 18.50 percent.
Bankers acceptances eased to 18.25 and 17.50 percent (buying and selling respectively) from 18.50 and 17.80 percent while call money fluctuated between 17.50 and 17.75 percent from 19 percent.
